teaser.en: The garden *tungudza* has a wild cousin, *mtungudza koma*, that is used in medicine instead of the cooking pot.

summary.en: *Tungudza* is the African eggplant or garden egg, a bushy plant with small round fruits. Both the fruit and the leaves are cooked.

about.en: *Tungudza* is a bushy plant with broad leaves and small star-shaped flowers, white or pale purple. The fruits are small and round, like little eggs, and may be green, white, yellow or orange-red.

where.en: It is grown in home gardens on the south coast.

uses.en: Both the fruit and the leaves are cooked.

names.en: The fruit is *tungudza* and the plant *mtungudza*. The wild *Solanum incanum* is called *mtungudza koma*, the wild *tungudza*, and is used in medicine. Swahili calls the garden kind *ngogwe* or *tungudza*. In English it is African eggplant or garden egg. The name covers two species, *Solanum macrocarpon* and *S. aethiopicum*.

reason.en: Its wild relative, used in medicine

sources: Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: An ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD diss., Univ. Bayreuth (Appendix III & Table G.2) https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
